audits.title: 859 Improving Accuracy of Admission Notes Over A Four-Year Period Within an Orthopaedic Trauma Ward: A Four-Cycle Audit
audits.standard: Royal College of Surgeons standards for documentation
audits.setting: Orthopaedic trauma ward, Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh

cycle1.result: Initially only two criteria had above 95% compliance; 'note signed' 60%, 'date stamp' 66%, 'contact number' 0%.

audits.intervention: Educational posters; change from handwritten to online admission forms; optimisation of the online proforma with further education.

cycle2.period: Fourth cycle, one year after the third
cycle2.result: All criteria documented in over 95% after further education and proforma modification.

audits.other_findings: Four cycles: posters improved 'note signed' (60% to 96%); moving online improved 'date stamp' (66% to 100%) and 'contact number' (0% to 34%) but reduced 'time recorded' (18% to 0%) and 'name and grade' (74% to 26%).
audits.citation: McCann C, Mackenzie S, White T. 859 Improving Accuracy of Admission Notes Over A Four-Year Period Within an Orthopaedic Trauma Ward: A Four-Cycle Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab134.495.

audits.title: Use of a Pediatric Admission Booklet Significantly Improves the Comprehensiveness of Admission Documentation: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: 17 admission documentation standards based on Royal College of Physicians clerking standards and RCPCH/PRSB digital record standards; aim to raise average compliance from 59% to above 90%
audits.setting: Bristol Royal Hospital for Children; tertiary paediatric hospital (paediatric medicine, surgery and orthopaedics)

cycle1.result: Blank continuation sheets: 5 of 17 standards >90%, none 100%; medications 48%, allergies 47%, social history 36%, responsible consultant 8%, accompanying adult 24%, observations 38%.

audits.intervention: Specialty-specific colour-coded pre-printed admission booklets with prompts and tick boxes (medicine, surgery, orthopaedics), introduced March 2019 with teaching at junior doctor handovers.

cycle2.period: From March 2019 (first 40 booklet admissions per specialty)
cycle2.result: Average 33% absolute improvement (P < 0.01); 12 of 17 standards >90% and 4 at 100%; medications 99%, allergies 93%, consultant 88%, accompanying adult 68%, observations 52%.

audits.other_findings: Observations (52%) and investigations (70%) remained poorly documented. Examination findings and plans were already well documented and changed little.
audits.citation: Beverstock A, Lewis C, Bruce D, Barnes J, Kelly A. Use of a Pediatric Admission Booklet Significantly Improves the Comprehensiveness of Admission Documentation: A Quality Improvement Project. Pediatr Qual Saf. 2020;5(1):e247. doi:10.1097/pq9.0000000000000247. PMID: 32190793.

cycle2.result: Proforma notes: consultant on call 100% (p=0.0005); time of injury 100% (p=0.0001); associated injury 100% (p=0.0001); smoking 100% (p=0.0001); alcohol 94% (p=0.0001); vital signs 70% (p=0.0001); other systems 74% (p=0.0001).

audits.other_findings: Admitting doctor grade documentation fell from 92% to 82% and vital signs remained incomplete at 70%. A poll of 16 Irish units found admission proforma use in only 18.8%.

audits.title: A Standardised Clerking Proforma Improves the Perceived Satisfaction of Healthcare Professionals and Leads to Better Documentation.
audits.standard: Royal College of Surgeons and Professional Record Standards Body (PRSB) documentation standards
audits.setting: Surgical assessment unit, major trauma centre (University Hospitals Plymouth)

cycle1.result: Information was missing in the categories of responsible consultant, medication history, allergy status and differential diagnosis.

audits.intervention: Structured Surgical Assessment Proforma introduced (PDSA cycle, designed after a clinician survey).

cycle2.result: Of 45 assessment criteria, 38 improved (23 significantly; p<0.05), two showed no change and five were reduced (two significantly; p<0.05). Documentation rates in nine categories improved by over 50%.

audits.other_findings: Post-proforma survey: 73% of doctors and 86% of allied health professionals agreed documentation improved; 100% of AHPs said it improved handover.

audits.title: The use of a pro forma to improve quality in clerking vascular surgery patients.
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians 2009 standards for admission clerking documentation
audits.setting: Vascular surgery ward, large tertiary referral centre, Barts Health NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Presenting complaint absent in 19%; past surgical history absent in 45%; drug history 72%, doses and frequency 41%, allergy status 75%; family history 19%; systems enquiry 12%; vascular examination 59%, pulses 46%; observations 31%; VTE assessment 73%

audits.intervention: Clerking pro forma based on RCP guidance (with AMTS, VTE, ABPI, investigations and nil-by-mouth sections), junior doctor education and a named FY1 lead per cohort

cycle2.result: Sustained improvement in record keeping; observations recorded in 62% (significant increase); non-significant improvements in nil-by-mouth status and prior investigations

audits.other_findings: At PDSA 1 (30 clerkings, 28 on the pro forma) most domains improved significantly (p <0.05), but observations were 42% and nil-by-mouth documentation fell. A later check of 23 acute-take clerkings not using the pro forma was as poor as baseline.
audits.citation: Kentley J, Fox A, Taylor S, Hassan Y, Filipek A. The use of a pro forma to improve quality in clerking vascular surgery patients. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2016;5(1):u210642.w4280. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u210642.w4280. PMID: 27418964.

audits.title: Checklist to aid young physicians managing obstetric emergencies in rural India: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.standard: Completeness of 31 agreed data points on first information sheets (items based on hospital policy and Ministry of Health guidelines); aim >90% completeness
audits.setting: Obstetric emergency, Sub-District Hospital Ballabgarh (secondary care, AIIMS New Delhi rural health project)

cycle1.result: Mean first information sheet completeness 73.95%; 1 of 12 (8.33%) fully complete.

audits.intervention: PDSA cycles: education session for interns; wall notes of required data points; a printed antenatal care (ANC) admission checklist, then implemented with shift-wise training and nursing officers printing it each shift.

cycle2.result: Mean completeness 86.34% (p<0.001); 16 of 65 (24.62%) fully complete (p=0.2); ANC checklist used in 69.72% of sheets.

audits.other_findings: Physical examination items improved most; high-risk pregnancy documentation rose from 0% to 56.66% (17/30). Sheets with the checklist were more complete than those without (87.74% vs 74.42%).
audits.citation: Puntambekar V, Sharma AK, Yadav K, Kumar R. Checklist to aid young physicians managing obstetric emergencies in rural India: a quality improvement initiative. BMJ Open Qual. 2021;10(Suppl 1):e001435. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2021-001435. PMID: 34344735.
